item.title: ‘Not my Administrator’: David Connolly sworn in as Administrator at Parliament as public protest outside
item.description: David Connolly was sworn in as the next Administrator of the Northern Territory Friday morning in a red carpet ceremony, starting his tenure by saying he wanted to thank the Larrakia people and "pay respects to them all, past and present", while outside a Larrakia elder was arrested at what was a peaceful protest of more than a hundred people, which descended into brief chaos after the arrest.

item.title: Opinion: Governance and financial failures at CDU examined
item.description: As Charles Darwin University launches a duplicated medical program amid mounting losses and large debt, and in the wake of a widening training scandal involving the carpentry apprenticeship which saw the vice-chancellor resign leading to a possible class action, there are serious concerns that both the executive leadership and the university council have failed in their oversight of the institution, writes Dr Don Fuller.

item.title: Swearing-in of David Connolly the latest indignity for the Northern Territory
item.description: EDITORIAL: David Connolly made the whole affair worse on Friday morning in his first speech as Administrator with his condescending attitude while his supporters surely cringed when he attempted to speak in language and talked about his great and deep respect for Indigenous culture. We all knew it was a lie, which made it all the more grotesque.

item.title: NT Criminal Court list – with charges – Mar 03
item.description: The 283 names facing criminal courts in the Northern Territory for Tuesday, March 03, 2026. This list includes all the charges.

item.title: CDU pulls plug on London campus after blowing $2 million on uni council approved debacle
item.description: Outgoing CDU vice-chancellor Scott Bowman's legacy of a London campus has been scrapped after the university spent nearly $2 million on the flawed project and hired three of Mr Bowman's mates with taxpayer money to run it, the university has said, while questions to its council about how it allowed the proposal to proceed have been ignored.

item.title: Palmerston stolen car crime spree, attempted carjacking in shopping centre car park over weekend
item.description: A 30-year-old man was arrested Sunday morning with an "edged weapon" in his possession after he allegedly approached a woman heading to her car in an underground car park at a Palmerston shopping centre before assaulting her while trying to take her car, NT Police said.

item.title: High school staff member assaulted by student: Police
item.description: A 15-year-old male has been arrested in connection to the alleged assault of a female staff member at Tennant Creek High School on Monday, NT Police said.

item.title: Woman hospitalised, two arrested over pedestrian strike in Tennant Creek
item.description: A woman suffering "visible head injuries" is in hospital in a serious condition after being struck by a car in Tennant Creek this morning, with two men in their 20s later arrested, NT Police said.

item.title: ‘I was a naive cattleman’: Connolly attempts to explain social media posts in new interview
item.description: Administrator David Connolly says he was a "naive cattleman" mixed up in the high stakes world of "agri-politics" when he made controversial social media comments disparaging Aboriginal people, women and the LGBTQI community and joked about domestic violence and date rape, which he said was "pastoral world" talk, while his former employer at Tipperary Station has provided some insight into why he left the station manager role last year.

item.title: AirAsia cancels two Darwin flight services
item.description: AirAsia will discontinue its Darwin to Bali and Kuala Lumpur routes less than a year after launching due to operating below a 70 per cent load factor, making them economically unsustainable, the company has indicated, while the NT Government has pledged to review its taxpayer-funded air subsidy scheme in the wake of the cancelled routes.
